newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Peru rebel leader's mother to sue Japan.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel leader's mother to sue Japan.

text.p: The mother of dead Peruvian rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini plans to make a legal claim against Japan for the execution of her son, an Argentine newspaper reported on Sunday.

"My son was killed on Japanese territory," Felicitas Cartolini told Argentina's Clarin in an interview from France where she lives with Cerpa's two sons. "And I am going to make a legal claim against the government of Japan."

Peru's military stormed the Japanese ambassador's mansion on April 22, freeing all but one of 72 hostages held there for 126 days. Troops killed all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels. Japan's government was not notified of the attack.
Under international law embassies are considered to be the territory of the country whose diplomatic mission is housed there rather than the territory of the host nation.
"I know he was executed. One of the hostages, the agriculture minister said so, and there are other hostages that also witnessed this," she said.

News reports last week suggested some rebels tried to surrender to save their lives. Peru's government denied there were any surrenders or executions and that all the rebels died in combat with soldiers.
Felicitas Cartolini said she was making the claim with the help of international human rights organisations.
Together with the families of the other MRTA rebels, Cartolini is asking organisations to carry out forensic tests to determine the circumstances of the deaths.
